en: Eight cremation grounds are described. To the east is the cremation ground named Caṇḍa. There, upon a *harītakī* tree, resides the one of great supernatural power (*maharddhika*) named Caṇḍogra, who has the face of an elephant and is white in color. At the foot of the tree is the directional lord Indra, yellow in color, holding a vajra and a threatening gesture (*tarjanī*) in his right and left hands respectively; he is mounted upon the white Airāvata. The *nāga* here is Vāsuki, the color of nectar (*pīyūṣa*). The cloud is named Garjita. (1)

In the north is the seat named Gahvara. There, at the foot of the Bodhi tree, is the one named Gahvara, possessing great supernatural power (*maharddhika*), with a human face and yellow in color. At the base of the tree is Kubera, the Lord of the Quarter, yellow in color, holding the gesture of fearlessness (*abhaya*) and a mace (*gadā*) in his right and left hands respectively. He is mounted upon a treasure (*nidhi*), is short in stature, and is accompanied by the Naga Takṣaka, who is red in color, and the cloud named Pūrṇatā. || 2 ||

In the west is the cremation ground named Jvālākulakaraṅka. There, upon an Aśoka tree, resides the one of great supernatural power named Jvālākulakaraṅka. He has a makara face and is red in color. At the foot of the tree is the directional lord Vāruṇa, who is white and has a nāga as his seat. With his right and left hands, he holds a threatening gesture (*tarjanī*) and a nāga-noose. The nāga here is Karkkoṭaka, who is dark blue; the cloud is called Ghorā. (3)

To the south is the cremation ground named Vibhīṣaṇa. There, upon a *vibhītaka* tree, resides one named Vibhīṣaṇa, who possesses great supernatural power (*maharddhika*), has the face of a buffalo, and is black in color. At the foot of the tree is the directional lord Yama, who is black. With his right and left arms, he holds a staff and a noose; he is mounted upon a buffalo. Here, the *nāga* is Padma, who is white, and the cloud is named Āvarta. 4.

In the southeast is the cremation ground named Lakṣmīvana. There, upon a karañja tree, dwells the one named Lakṣmīvana, who has the face of a goat, is red in color, and possesses great supernatural power (*maharddhika*). At the foot of the tree is the Lord of the Directions, Vahni (Fire), red in color, holding a rosary and a water-pot (*kamaṇḍalu*) in his right and left hands respectively. He is seated upon a goat. Here, the *nāga* is Mahāpadma, white as a lotus stalk (*mṛṇāla*). The cloud is called Ghanākhya. 5.

In the southwest is the cremation ground named Ghorā. There, upon a *parkaṭī* tree, resides the one of great supernatural power named Ghora, who has a human face and is black in color. At the foot of the tree is the directional lord Nairṛti, a *rākṣasa*, who is black and holds a threatening gesture (*tarjanī*) and a severed head (*muṇḍa*) in his right and left hands; he is seated upon his vehicle. Here, the *nāga* is Ananta, blue in color, and the cloud is known as Tṛpurāṇa. (6)

In the northwest is the cremation ground named Kilakilārava. There, beneath a tree, is the one of great supernatural power (maharddhika) named Kilikilārava, who has a monkey face and is smoke-colored. At the foot of the tree is the guardian of the direction, Pavana (the Wind), mounted on a deer, holding two wind-banners with his right and left hands, and white in color. The *nāga* here is Kulika, who is variegated in color; the cloud is known as Varṣa. || 7 ||

In the northeast is the cremation ground named Aṭṭaṭṭahāsa. There, upon a banyan tree of great supernatural power, resides the white bull-faced one named Aṭṭaṭṭahāsa. At the foot of the tree is the Lord of the Quarters, Bhūteśa, smoke-colored and mounted upon a bull; he holds a trident and a skull-cup in his right and left hands respectively. Here, the serpent is yellow and has five heads, and the cloud is known as Caṇḍa. || 8 ||

All the guardians of the directions have human faces and two arms; they are nāgas with seven hoods, wearing garlands formidable with fangs, capable of assuming forms at will, and their clouds are of every color.
Hari resides in the *abhayā* tree, [and] Niḥkaruṇa in the *bhūta* tree;

Varuṇa is in the *aśoka*, Kubera in the *bodhisikhariṇī*; Śikhin is in the *karañja*, the night-wanderer (*rātrimaṭa*) in the *latāparkaṭī*, Pavana in the tree called *kakubha*, and Bhūteśa resides in the *nyagrodha*.
Caṇḍogra, Gahvara, Jvālākula, Karaṅkaka,
and Vibhīṣaṇa are stationed on the left in the directions starting from the east; Aṭaṭṭahāsa is in the northeast, and Lakṣmīvana is in the southeast.
Terrible darkness in the southwest, and the sound of "kili-kili" in the northwest—
these eight cremation grounds within the diamond lattice (*vajrapañjara*) should be meditated upon with diligence by the glorious *Hevajra* yogins.
To the east are the trees Sirīṣa, Aśvattha, Kaṅkeli, and Cūta;
also the Vaṭa, Karañja, and the king of the Parkaṭī creepers.
Furthermore, there are Indra, Dhanada, the Lord of Nāgas, and the Sovereign Yama.
Īśāna, Hutāśa, the lord of the rākṣasas, and the lord of the winds;
Vāsuki, Takṣaka, Karkoṭaka, Padma, Mahāpadma, Huluhulu, Kulika, and Saṃkhapāla.
Garjita, Ghūrṇita, Ghorāvarta, and Ghananūpura—
these are the fierce lords of the clouds who rain down.

The trees, the guardians of the directions, the lords of the nāgas, and the lords of the clouds—these clouds are to be visualized as having the colors black, white, dark grey, pale, red, yellow, green, and variegated.
